sampling_model.design: The schedule \(g_n\), wedge \(\Omega_n\), dimensions, rank, and noise variance are fixed and known. The rate-optimal constructive theorem is restricted to the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask.
sampling_model.units: The parameter at index \(n\) is the tuple \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\) in \(\Theta_n\), not an observational equivalence class of outcome laws.
sampling_model.treatment: The matrix \(D_n\) is supported on \(W_n\); the counterfactual target is the \(L_n\) coordinate of the same experiment index.
sampling_model.overlap: The full class imposes quantitative observed-subblock Grams. The proved rate certificate uses the single balanced chart, for which the row and column anchors are the observed half-panels and synchronization is the identity.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The total procedure randomizes the observed vector into independent Gaussian pilot and inference copies, uses total spectral and pseudoinverse conventions, applies one-step block transport, and calibrates an explicitly ordered conditional Gaussian nuclear quantile plus the homogeneous observable remainder \(\mathscr R_n^{(2)}\). The stable branch requires \(\widehat\delta_n\ge4\tau_n\); every failure triggers a deterministic covering radius. The \(\sigma\sqrt n\) expected-radius guarantee is asserted only for the balanced one-chart benchmark.
sampling_model.randomness: Under \(\mathbb P_{\vartheta,n}\), cells are independent \(\mathcal N(L_{n,it}+D_{n,it},\sigma^2)\); the main observed experiment is its \(P_{\Omega_n}Y_n\) marginal \(\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}\).

Their Theorems 1--2 give entrywise Gaussian inference and a matching scalar instance-wise lower bound under row- and column-side subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise and noise restrictions, and target-local leverage conditions, without this note's global-incoherence condition. Only a lower-bound or converse comparison on an explicitly embedded common subclass transfers upward by inclusion; no constructive upper bound transfers between the classes.
Theorems 1 and 4 derive nuclear detection boundaries and nuclear-diameter rank-adaptation impossibility in Gaussian trace regression.
Theorems 3.4--3.5 characterize worst-case Frobenius residual error for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block.
Proposition 2 derives tall-wide common-component error expansions under strong factors in the observed subblocks.
The paper constructs prescribed-coverage intervals for individual effects and bilinear functionals under staggered adoption.
The paper gives rate-optimal recovery and asymptotic normality for average treatment effects under general intervention patterns.

body.tldr: The paper indexes the Gaussian panel experiment by admissible tuples \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\), so the latent counterfactual matrix remains part of the experiment index even when tuples induce the same observed law. Its principal fixed-interior benchmark is the balanced rank-one L-mask frontier \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\sqrt n\) for \(\mu>1\), established by an all-procedure lower bound and a total polynomial-time one-block certificate whose conditional Gaussian, finite-simulation, homogeneous Taylor, and fallback contributions are controlled separately. Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} is the boundary companion for every \(0<\kappa\le1\): at \(\mu=1\), both normalized balanced overlap Grams equal one, the frontier is \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\) when \(s_-<s_+\), and it is exactly zero when \(s_-=s_+\), even though \(\mathfrak R_n\ge\sigma\sqrt{2n}\). Thus neither the fixed-interior frontier nor a tangent-modulus lower comparison extends to the saturated boundary. The shrinking-incoherence layer and arbitrary admissible interior multi-chart wedges remain open in Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge}. The diffuse-weight ATT interval is only a coverage-valid duality corollary.

project_justification.gap: Yan and Wainwright impose low rank on one untreated-potential-outcome matrix \(M^\star\); post-treatment observations are not jointly modeled with that untreated potential outcome. Their scalar theory uses row- and column-side subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise and noise restrictions, and target-local leverage conditions, but not this note's global-incoherence condition. Consequently the two model classes are not interchangeable: only a lower-bound or converse proved on an explicitly embedded common subclass transfers upward by inclusion, while no constructive upper bound transfers across the classes. More broadly, sharp staggered-panel inference remains coordinatewise or functional-specific, whereas global matrix confidence theory uses random or isotropic measurements; no located result gives this note's tuple-indexed honest nuclear ball under a deterministic adoption wedge together with both the fixed-interior frontier and the saturated-incoherence boundary characterization.
project_justification.niche: Known rank, independent Gaussian cells, strong factors, global incoherence, and quantitative overlap Grams isolate a deterministic-wedge confidence problem with a genuine phase split: the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask has a fixed interior regime \(\mu>1\) and a saturated boundary \(\mu=1\), where the normalized overlap Grams equal one for every allowed \(0<\kappa\le1\).
project_justification.fill: For the balanced rank-one L-mask, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} proves the \(\sigma\sqrt n\) two-sided frontier only in the fixed-interior regime \(\mu>1\). Its note-specific total spectral certificate is audited term by term, including conditional Gaussian calibration, finite simulation, the homogeneous Taylor remainder, and fallback; no constructive result is imported from a different comparator class. Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} proves the full \(\mu=1\) phase change for arbitrary \(0<\kappa\le1\): the radius is of order \(\sigma\) if \(s_-<s_+\), is zero if \(s_-=s_+\), and is negligible relative to the unrestricted tangent modulus. Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge} separates the unresolved shrinking-incoherence layer from the arbitrary interior multi-chart wedge frontier.

body.related_work: Yan and Wainwright provide the closest computational and inferential comparison. Their setup imposes low rank on one untreated-potential-outcome matrix \(M^\star\), while post-treatment observations are not jointly modeled with that untreated potential outcome. Their four-block SVD theory gives non-asymptotic entrywise Gaussian approximations and matching scalar lower bounds under row- and column-side subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise and noise restrictions, and target-local leverage conditions; it does not impose this note's global-incoherence condition. Accordingly, only a lower-bound or converse comparison established on an explicitly embedded common subclass transfers upward by inclusion; neither their constructive upper bounds nor this note's certificate transfer across the classes. Bai and Ng supply the tall-wide factor-rotation architecture and asymptotic counterfactual expansions under strong observed subblocks; block transport is used here as a supporting identification lemma. Carpentier and Nickl supply testing reductions for honest nuclear confidence diameter in isotropic Gaussian trace regression, with rank adaptation as their central obstruction. Capponi and Stojnic analyze worst-case Frobenius residuals for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block, a procedure-specific target distinct from the uniformly honest radius. Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan study debiased uncertainty quantification under random sampling, where sampling isometry replaces deterministic block geometry. Chatterjee characterizes qualitative recoverability under arbitrary deterministic masks, and Arkhangelsky and Imbens organize factor and assignment-pattern distinctions without a global honest matrix radius. Against these comparators, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} supplies the fixed-\(\mu>1\) interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier, whereas Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} shows for every \(0<\kappa\le1\) that the \(\mu=1\) frontier is only order \(\sigma\), or exactly zero at the known-level elbow, despite an order-\(\sigma\sqrt n\) unrestricted tangent modulus. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright and Farias, Li, and Peng remain functional-specific benchmarks; the ATT proposition claims coverage transfer and no optimal-length comparison.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The \(\sigma\sqrt n\) certificate and minimax frontier are confined to the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask with fixed \(\mu>1\). The displayed multi-chart synchronization is a total computational construction, but no rate or honesty theorem is asserted for a general connected wedge. A broader interior theorem requires a uniform post-synchronization envelope and nuclear-mask amplification bound together with a same-class packing preserving exact rank, strong factors, global incoherence, every chartwise overlap, and controlled observed-law divergence. Separately, neither the fixed-interior packing nor the saturated-boundary sign reduction is uniform in a shrinking-incoherence layer \(\mu_n\downarrow1\); Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge} records both unresolved regimes without positing an interpolation rate.
body.honest_scope: The balanced rank-one two-sided frontier for fixed \(\mu>1\), its total one-block spectral certificate, the full \(\mu=1\) boundary characterization for every \(0<\kappa\le1\), and the diffuse-weight ATT coverage corollary are the proved deliverables. At the boundary the frontier is order \(\sigma\) when \(s_-<s_+\) and zero when the common level is known through \(s_-=s_+\); neither result is an extension of the interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) claim. The exact conditional Gaussian term, Monte Carlo inflation, homogeneous Taylor remainder, and fallback contribution are separately bounded at the interior benchmark scale. Both the shrinking-incoherence layer and a rate-optimal honest certificate with a matching all-procedure lower bound for arbitrary admissible interior wedges remain open in Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge}. No theorem is asserted for a multi-chart connected wedge, unknown rank, approximate low rank, dependent or heteroskedastic errors, adaptive adoption, or optimal ATT length.
